candidate: Use one autonomous data-state update U repeatedly, with a fixed shared bijective state encoding, to implement different word operations
version_a: Operation-specific constant repetition counts; no state-dependent count
version_b: Allow operation- and state-dependent nonnegative counts; no auxiliary data state, no mode input to U, no instruction-specific re-encoding
primary_gate: Exact representability, then number of applications of U rather than interpreter wall time
checks: All 256 maps on four states and their entire finite power sequences
All 65536 ordered pairs of four-state maps
Every directed full cycle on 2,4,8 labeled states, modulo rotation
All 256 source maps on four states through each full cycle with state-dependent counts
controls: add one and add two are fixed powers of successor
commuting does not imply sharing an iterative generator
arbitrary finite maps are realizable with data-dependent stopping on a full cycle
decision: Reject constant counts if target operations do not commute; reject a single-word autonomous variable-duration implementation if required average microsteps grow as 2^(w-1)
attacker: Full program, public input and arbitrary traces allowed, but no attack resistance is inferred from feasibility checks
